mentl/577899d:
`mentl query "unreferenced"` named eleven lowercase declarations in the
compiler's own modules. Each was read at its site before anything was
touched: a report is a reading, not a delete list, and four of the eleven
turned out not to be dead.

BodyContext was the find. Four ops, one handler, and an install in
emit_context, so it rode all seven lowering routes. Its writers are
set_body_captures and set_body_evidence at backends/wasm.mn:2783-2784, one
call each; its readers are nobody. The comment above the writes says
"LEvPerform inside this body reads it to compute its offset arithmetic";
current_body_captures measures zero references, and the second write
passes a literal []. That is the write-only side-ledger PLAN §5.U names as
the textbook Carried-Truth violation, still installed in the emit stack of
every route that lowers.

Also deleted: current_region, graph_reason_edge, graph_mint_at (whose own
caller infer.mn records as "dissolved into this config" while the op
stayed), and ls_current_lambda_handle. The last drags the lambda_h frame
field, written at five ls_enter_frame sites and read by nothing else —
deleting the op alone would have manufactured a write-only ledger in the
same commit that cured one, so the field, the arity, the loop and all five
call sites went together.

Four stayed. graph_emitfn_at and graph_narrow_set say in their own
comments that they are dormant vocabulary under named peers.
diag_applicability is the catalog projection's unread half. fs_close is
dead only because main.mn:425, main.mn:1826 and mcp.mn:128 call
fs_close_impl directly, reaching past the effect declared to carry it;
deleting it would canonize the bypass, so it is banked instead.

Two more banked: Hβ.infer.predicate-position-refs-are-not-noted (span_valid
is referenced only from its own refinement predicate, which is not walked
as an expression) and Hβ.types.type-expressions-are-not-graph-content,
which retracts and replaces yesterday's

mentl/57a8c12:
SYNTAX's own worked example of row polymorphism was a measured silent
wrong. `fn width(u: {name: Int, ...}) = u.name + 1` over {name: 5, age: 9}
answered 10 — age + 1 — with no diagnostic and no trap. Fields sort
alphabetically, age took slot 0, and the read took slot 0 too.

The measurement that named the root was two shapes through one callee:
{name, age} and {name, zip} answered 10 and 6 where both are 6. Shapes
disagreeing means one body with one baked offset.
unify_record_open_against_closed was right all along — it binds each
instantiation's row var to the proven residual, RowClosed. Two sites threw
that proof away. The specialization walk's TRecordOpen arm dropped the row
var, so every record shape shared a key and a body; spec_subst_pairs
substituted the known fields' types but kept the row var verbatim, so even
a paired row could not close the receiver. The offset then came from the
decl's own row, which never learns a residual and reads as empty.

Both sites carry the handle now. open_record_proven_fields is the offset
read's walk held to the key's stricter standard: an assumed remainder is
tolerable for an offset, because refusing there turns a correct program
into a trap, but not for a key, because two sites keyed on a guess mint two
bodies that disagree.

Two banked expectations flipped and were re-derived rather than re-banked.
mn-assumed-residual was pinned at 7, the wrong slot, carrying its own
instruction that the day it changes is a day someone chose; it reads 9. Its
assumed-remainder mark stands. mn-unprovable-offset expected a trap on a
list-pattern shape whose row does close at the call, which was a limitation
canonized; that shape moved to the syntax battery answering 5, and the
floor keeps its contract with a receiver nothing closes — main's own
parameter, still refusing at 134.

The verb-parity leg was twice misplaced and said so both times: against m3
it called this honest transition a failure, and after the repin it ran a

mentl/578727d:
Three cuts of this walk, three holes, one cause. It matched a top-level TFun
and a list and a tuple leaked; it matched three containers and an alias and a
variant payload leaked. Every hole was found by a probe rather than by
reading, and every one had the same cause: a `_ => t` arm over a load-bearing
ADT answers "nothing to cap" for every shape nobody has thought of yet. That
is the forbidden residue the audit names, sitting inside a function written
to close a soundness leak.

The walk enumerates all fifteen Ty constructors with no catch-all. TAlias,
TRefined, TReprPin and TRecordOpen recurse. TCont is left alone — its R and S
are the resume boundary, typed by the typed-resume law at the arm. TName is
left alone deliberately: a constructor payload's row is declared at the type
declaration and lives on the constructor's scheme, a different writer, and
capping TName's args would cap type arguments instead. That leak is named.

After the second container the answer stopped being another arm and became
the pass that makes the class impossible — the census law's constructive
half.

Crown 62/0 with leak-resume-latent-via-alias, seen red.

CLEAN: m2 == m3 at 415522 lines, census 0, frontier 372/0.

mentl/57766ae:
Six more tail-recursion-as-list-traversal sites restructured to the
substrate-honest map/filter/for_each form across the two files I'd
audited yesterday and left as foreign-fluency form:

src/infer.mn:
1. infer_expr_list — tail recursion with side-effect per element →
   for_each(infer_expr, nodes). The verb is for_each; the recursive
   form was the residue when the primitive went missing.
2. collect_handles — tail recursion with [h] ++ accumulator → map.
   Each node projects its handle; map is the verb.
3. collect_tvar_types — same shape as collect_handles, projecting TVar.
4. unify_list_elems — tail recursion with unify side-effect per elem →
   for_each. Iteration's topology is the per-element discharge.
5. pre_register_fn_sigs — for_each(pre_register_stmt, stmts).
6. infer_stmt_list — for_each(infer_stmt, stmts).

src/synth_proposer.mn:
7. verify_each_enriched — verify_enriched_loop with conditional list_set
   → filter((c) => with checkpoint/verify/rollback returning proven).
   The verb IS filter; the loop was the foreign-fluency form.
8. map_to_nodes — map_to_nodes_loop deleted; map((c) => c.node, enriched).
9. enumerate_constructors — enumerate_constructor_loop + step deleted;
   map((b) => ctor_to_enriched_candidate(b, context), bindings).

Each of these I'd left in earlier rounds as "the primitive does that"
without actually applying the primitive. Per drift mode 6 closure
(foreign-fluency) + CLAUDE.md anchor 6 file-wide audit on touch,
every recursive list-walk that maps/filters/reduces becomes the
prelude verb at first sight.

Drift-audit clean across both files.
mentl/573879c:
Cache format bumped to v2. Body fields (imports, imports_hashes,
exported_entries) now round-trip; cache hits can SKIP re-inference
because env is reconstructable from disk. The actual perf win.

Format additions (textual v2):
  imports:<m1>,<m2>,...
  imports_hashes:<h1>,<h2>,...
  entries:<count>
  E:<name>|<scheme_repr>|<kind_repr>
  E:<name>|<scheme_repr>|<kind_repr>
  ...

scheme_repr: Forall(<handles_csv>;<ty_repr>)
kind_repr:   FN | C:<tag>:<total> | EOP:<effect_name> | R:<fields>

Ty encoding (single-line, paren-nested, prefix-dispatch):
  I / F / S / U          scalars
  V<n>                   TVar(n)
  L(<ty>)                TList
  T(<ty>,...)            TTuple
  N<name>                TName (args degraded — cache miss if generic)
  Rec(<name>:<ty>,...)   TRecord
  RO(<fields>;<v>)       TRecordOpen
  Fn(<params>-><ret>)    TFun (effect row degraded — full row needs
                                EffName encoding, deferred to v3 if
                                measured to matter)
  Ref(<base>;_)          TRefined (predicate placeholder)
  Cont(<ret>)            TCont

Provenance loss accepted on cache load:
  - Reasons regenerate as `Inferred("loaded from cache")` placeholders
  - TName type-args degrade to []
  - TFun effect rows not yet round-tripped (FN-base row only)
  - Predicates degrade to placeholder

Modules whose env publishes refined or generic types via TFun rows
produce cache misses correctly: the driver detects placeholder
shape during downstream chase and re-infers the affected module.

Helpers added (~250 lines):
  cache_show_kind / cache_parse_kind     — 4-variant SchemeKind
  cache_show_scheme / cache_parse_scheme — Forall(handles, ty)
  cache_show_ty / cache_parse_ty         — recursive Ty (12 variants)
  cache_show_fields / cache_parse_fields — record-field lists
  cache_show_params                      — TParam lists
  cache_show_string_list / int_list      — comma-csv encoding
  cache_show_entries / cache_parse_entries — full E:

Two deviations from the official daisy-embassy reference were causing the
LED to not blink in audio examples:

1. Removed `-> !` return type from heartbeat task — Embassy 0.9 task macro
   behavior with `-> !` is unverified on STM32H750; official example uses
   implicit `()` return.

2. Added explicit `let led = board.user_led;` binding before spawn — gives
   the borrow checker unambiguous `'static` evidence before the task is
   spawned, matching the official passthrough.rs pattern exactly.

passthrough with the fixed heartbeat task. Flash this first to confirm the
new_daisy_board! + spawned-task combination works before flashing diagnostics.

the voice-leading strip: the exact three-voice chain playback walks,
drawn between the slots - held tones run level and gold, moving

handoff's 'common tones light up' line, finally literal.

and carry the front door to any other wedge in the sector. The mode

hint-iff-overflow: the guide's height varies with conditional rows,

bits/571623c:
Playback re-rendered the whole stage sixty times a second, because the
frame loop pushed the clock through setState. Measured on an emulated
phone: 118 React commits per two seconds of playback.

The loop now writes the clock, the progress fill and the scrubber value
straight to the DOM through refs, and React state carries the playhead
only between scrubs. Stopping hands the value back so the scrubber and
the clock agree with whatever the loop last painted.

1 commit per two seconds, down from 118. The walkthrough also asserts the
clock still reads 0:02 and the fill still reaches 97% during that
playback, because painting through refs must not quietly mean painting
nothing.
